revisits.note: T15 v0.4 '内部に秩序を詰める' (作者発注: 「虚を詰めるは内部の構造の作り方、表面を詰めるは表層の作り方。両者を混ぜ合わせる方法って考えられる？例えば内部にもコインやリングを詰める。いきなり有機的だと複雑すぎるからグリッドパターンとかシンプルなところから」). Two additions: (1) THREE NEW UnitKind values moved in from skin/field.ts's surface vocabulary: 'coin' (anchor+sub-point blob), 'flatRing' (nodes on a circle, opens a real hole above holeRatio~0.47), 'ring3d' (S-rings' own generateRingBalls torus, shared not copied). These are PACK-LOCAL COPIES of skin's buildCoinPoints/buildFlatRingPoints/buildRing3dPoints with the surface re-projection (projectToSurface) dropped — an internal unit has no surface to conform to, so points stay exactly in the anchor's tangent plane; generateRingBalls/rotatePoint themselves ARE imported (not copied) from rings/ring.ts, same 'share what has no reason to differ' split skin's own file header documents. All three orient via a `normal` supplied by the PLACEMENT mode (grid: axis-aligned; random: isotropic-random via a new randomNormal(rng), since random placement has no surface to read a normal from) — this is how 'コイン・平リングは向きを持つ' is satisfied in BOTH modes without inventing a second scheme. A new clampBallsToOuterRadius helper (uniform scale-toward-center) enforces the existing 'no ball exceeds the unit's outer sphere' contract for all three shapes, generalizing T14's cloud-only clamp. PackUnit gained an optional `normal` field (display/debug only — the balls are already baked in world space, replay never re-reads it). (2) NEW PlacementMode 'grid' (packUnitsGrid in field.ts) alongside the unchanged 'random' (T9's packUnitsGreedy, now selected explicitly via PackParams.placementMode, default 'random' so v0.3 recipes replay identically). Grid samples the cubic LATTICE itself (not random points): candidate lattice points → reject if the unit's outer sphere doesn't fit inside the host (same gap/penetration convention packUnitsGreedy already uses) → accept. New knobs: gridSpacing (unit size at ばらし=0 is DERIVED as spacing/2 − gap/2, reusing gap rather than minR/maxR — task doc lists only 間隔・千鳥・向き・ばらし as grid knobs, no separate size range), gridStagger (千鳥 — odd Z-layers offset by spacing/2 in X and Y; layer indexing is fixed to world Z regardless of gridAxis, a documented 仮決め so 'layer' has one unambiguous meaning), gridAxis (X/Y/Z base normal for oriented units, no effect on sphere/cloud), gridAlternate (alternates gridAxis↔nextAxis(gridAxis) on odd layers — verified coin units alternate between exactly {x:1,y:0,z:0} and {x:0,y:1,z:0} normals with gridStagger+gridAlternate both on). THE CENTRAL KNOB is gridScatter ('ばらし', 0..1, H1 UI per the task doc): at 0, every placement is exactly on-lattice, exactly gridAxis-oriented, exactly baseRadius (完了条件2, verified — 70 sphere units in a visibly regular row/column grid, screenshot taken). Rising toward 1 continuously injects (a) position jitter up to ±0.35·scatter·spacing per axis, (b) radius jitter up to ±0.35·scatter·baseRadius (clamped to [0.35,1.4]×baseRadius), (c) orientation = normalize(lerp(axisVector, freshIsotropicRandomVector, scatter)) — all three simultaneously, not a discrete on/off switch, satisfying 完了条件3's '連続に効く'. Screenshots taken at scatter=0 (crisp grid rows), 0.5 (visible size/position variance, rows still legible), 1.0 (size varies widely, rows barely legible, close to but not identical to true random packing — documented honestly in README as 'ばらし1は隣接構造をなお引きずる'). Determinism preserved: RNG seeded `${seed}#grid#${existingBallCount}` (same 'fold in current content' convention packUnitsGreedy already uses), consumed in fixed order per lattice point. History: NO NEW OP TYPE was needed — packUnits already carries the resulting PackUnit[] regardless of which algorithm produced it (T9's original design), so main.ts's runPack() just dispatches packUnitsGreedy vs packUnitsGrid by placementMode and records the SAME 'packUnits' op either way; UI's onPackParamChange was widened to accept boolean (gridStagger/gridAlternate) alongside the existing number|string. A GRID_POINT_CAP=40000 safety limit (not from the task doc, 仮決め) guards against a tiny spacing over a large host exploding the candidate count; hitting it sets stoppedEarly=true, same honesty convention as packUnitsGreedy's FAIL_LIMIT. VERIFIED: carve-mode ring3d grid (50 units, gridScatter=0.3) watertight at res64 (123,096 tris, 23 components — external shell + internal ring cavity walls, same topology fact T13 documented); fill-mode SAME packing watertight at res64 (114,620 tris, 25 components, honest separate-piece count since fill mode voids are literal printed pieces); carve-mode coin grid with BOTH stagger+alternate on (77 units) watertight at res64 (142,036 tris, 6 components). Zero regression: sphere+random packing on T13's exact default params reproduced 63/+44/+18 bit-for-bit across three consecutive packs (identical to the T13/T14 recorded runs). History export→import round-trip verified entries-identical (JSON string comparison, exportedAt excluded) on a 9-entry mixed carve/fill/grid/coin history. All 8 existing pages (index/gravity/sag/mpm/foam/rings/skin/pack) console-error-free; npm run build passes. KNOWN VERIFICATION GAP (environment, not a regression): canvas click-to-select could not be exercised via either the computer tool's real-coordinate click OR the documented real-PointerEvent-dispatch workaround in THIS session's automation environment — confirmed this is session-specific and NOT something introduced by this change by reproducing the identical failure on the UNMODIFIED, already-shipped skin.html (a grid-scanned dispatch over its whole canvas never triggered getSelectedPatchId() either). elementFromPoint confirmed every dispatch target was the CANVAS element (satisfying the letter of AGENTS §3's hit-test requirement); the underlying selection/whole-unit-deletion code path was verified instead via the __pack.selectUnit()/__pack.removeUnit() debug handles (same record()+afterMutation() call path a real click+Delete would trigger), confirming select-by-id and whole-unit removal (114→113 units) both work correctly downstream of picking. Left as a genuine open item for the author's own click-testing (visual confirmation item).

T14 v0.3 '雲を詰める' (作者発注「球体じゃなくて雲自体を入れ込むことは可能だろうか」= Y7第二補正の原文「ランダムな形態をパッキング」への回帰): the packed thing is promoted from a bare ball to a UNIT (field.ts's PackUnit = a group of balls + its own local blend k + a circumscribing sphere center/outerRadius). (1) Two unit kinds: 'sphere' (single ball; localK never enters the math, so sphere packing is numerically IDENTICAL to v0.2 — verified to the individual placement: first/second/third packs on default params gave 63/+44/+18, matching T13's recorded run exactly) and 'cloud' (3-10 balls generated growBalls-style from the packer's own rng walk, so every unit differs deterministically; same seed re-pack reproduces identical geometry, verified by JSON comparison excluding ids). minR/maxR are reinterpreted as bounds on the unit's CIRCUMSCRIBING radius; clearance between units is outer-sphere vs outer-sphere only ('精密判定はしない — 詰め方の偶然が価値' per the task doc, README documents the approximation). (2) S1 recipes can now be loaded as UNIT PROTOTYPES (loadCloudPrototype op; loadCloudPrototypeFromS1Recipe replays with S1's own replay()): each placed unit instances a randomly chosen prototype, normalized to the greedy radius (scale = maxR_at_point / prototype bounding-sphere radius, bounding sphere = centroid + max(dist+r), a conservative approximation) with a random Rodrigues rotation; verified 62/62 units carried the prototype's exact relative radii with 62 distinct orientations, localK scales with the unit. Loading a prototype auto-switches unitKind to cloud (recorded as a normal setPackParam so replay reproduces it). (3) Two-level smooth-min everywhere in lockstep: unitSdf (within-unit, localK) nested inside unitsFieldSdf (across-unit, roundK) on CPU (field/picking/meshExport) and in GLSL (new uUnitStart/uUnitCount/uUnitLocalK uniform arrays, VOID_MAX_UNITS=64 alongside VOID_MAX_BALLS=192; raymarch capacity is now exceeded when EITHER budget is, and the auto-switch-to-beads fires accordingly — with 3-10 balls per unit the ball budget is hit ~3-10x sooner, making the T13 auto-switch the common path for cloud packing; bead rendering measured 0.285ms/frame CPU-submission at 1404 balls, same benchmarkRender caveats as T13). (4) History ops packUnits/addUnit/removeUnit carry whole PackUnit data (unit boundaries included) — replay never re-runs any rng; export→import verified entries-identical with units, prototypes, mode and unit boundaries intact; unit-wise click-select (real PointerEvent) and Delete remove the WHOLE unit. (5) Gauges: estimateThinnestWall now measures between unit OUTER SPHERES (the same coarse proxy the packer enforced — honest in the right direction; per-ball would report tighter than anything the algorithm guaranteed), numerically identical to v0.2 for sphere units; estimateFillRatio deliberately stays per-ball (outer spheres would overstate material for clouds). UI notes the approximation next to the gauge. TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: (a) procedural cloud generation let the radius-spread factor (up to 1.3x) push a ball past the unit's outer sphere by ~0.024 (half the default gap!), silently eroding both the clearance contract and the penetration=0 closed-shell guarantee — fixed by clamping each ball's radius to (outerRadius - offset) after spread; re-verified maxOverflow=0 across a 69-unit pack. (b) fill-mode bounds (computeVoidsBounds) had NO margin, so the smooth-min union's bulge past the constituent balls' extents was clipped by the sampling box — fill-mode CLOUD meshes came back non-watertight at res 64 (T13's sphere-only fills never tripped this because a bounds-extreme sphere's outer tangent has no neighbor to blend with); fixed with the same margin formula cloud-sculpt's computeSamplingBounds uses, (roundK+maxLocalK) standing in for k; re-verified fill watertight at res 64 AND 96 (32/34 components, honest separate-piece count) and carve watertight at 64/96. Saturation prescription works for cloud units (8 consecutive packs → stoppedEarly + amber text; lowering minR 0.18→0.04 and gap→0.02 broke saturation with +45 units, exactly the prescription's claim). Verified in isolated Chrome (port 5185; author's 5174 untouched): unit-kind toggle and Pack button real-coordinate-clicked after elementFromPoint hit-tests; canvas unit-select via real PointerEvent dispatch (T9/T13's documented automation-env workaround; carve-mode outer-skin clicks correctly DESELECT since the hit is host skin, fill-mode clicks select the unit under the cursor); Delete key removed the whole 4-ball unit; all 8 pages console-error-free; npm run build passes.

T13 v0.2 '反転と改善': ported skin/S-surface-packing's T11-T12 fixes onto pack verbatim (same bug class, same fix, per author's explicit 'same考え方' framing). (1) New PackMode ('carve' = T9's host-minus-voids, default; 'fill' = new -- host becomes a placement-constraint-only mold, never part of the printed composite; compositeSdf's fill branch is simply fieldSdf(voids, roundK) with host completely ignored). packVoidsGreedy is UNCHANGED for fill mode (same greedy walk, same constraints -- host is still used to bound placement, exactly the author's 'behaves the same as before' requirement) -- only the composite/render/export layer branches on mode. New history op setMode (mirrors skin's identical op) records the toggle so export/import round-trips it; switching modes never re-runs the packer (same voids array, same ball data, just a different boolean formula over it) -- verified a plate<->window-style round trip via getMode()/exportJson(). (2) Fixed the exact same RNG-replay bug skin found: packVoidsGreedy's hashSeed(params.seed) replayed the identical sample sequence on every 詰める pass, so repeated packs added ~nothing; fixed with hashSeed(`${params.seed}#${voids.length}`), identical formula to skin's fix. Verified: 3 consecutive packs on identical params added 63/+44/+18 (not +0/+0). (3) Saturation prescription ported to ui.ts's setPackResult (amber .pack-saturated text: 'lower the min size or gap, attempts alone won't break saturation') -- verified triggering after repeated packs exhaust the geometry, then breaking saturation by lowering minR/gap. (4) Ported skin's T12 three-view system wholesale: renderer.ts gained updateBeads/updateBeadSelection (THREE.InstancedMesh, uncapped, host always drawn as a translucent 0.16-opacity backdrop -- this IS how the mold is shown in fill mode, since fill-mode raymarch deliberately never draws host) and setMeshOverlay (actual marching-tets triangle soup as a lit mesh); main.ts gained a three-way viewMode ('raymarch'|'beads'|'mesh') with the same auto-switch-to-beads-on-capacity-overflow + one-shot notice + mesh-invalidates-on-mutation rules as skin's identical mechanism. Void bead base color is mode-dependent per the task brief ('虚を暗色区別' in carve / '実を本体色で' in fill) -- VOID_BEAD_COLOR_CARVE (dark/cool, reads as cavity) vs VOID_BEAD_COLOR_FILL (same tone as host, reads as material); selection highlight color unchanged (shared cross-Study orange/gold, AGENTS §5). Selection remains visible in beads via cheap instanceColor recolor with no geometry rebuild, verified via grid-scanned real PointerEvent clicks. (5) meshExport.ts gained a self-contained countConnectedComponents (verbatim copy of skin/meshExport.ts's identical function, not imported, following the existing pack<->skin self-containment precedent) plus mode-aware bounds: carve keeps T9's host-derived sampling bounds, fill computes bounds directly from every void's own center+radius (computeVoidsBounds) since the host's extent is irrelevant/insufficient once patches can poke past it via penetration or manual placement. HONEST FINDING during verification (not a bug, a real topology fact worth documenting): carve mode's connected-component count for a fully closed shell (penetration=0, hasOpening=false) was NOT 1 as naively expected -- it was resolution-dependent (38/59/64 at res 64/96/128 for 63 sealed voids), because a solid with N sealed internal cavities has N+1 separate closed boundary surfaces (outer shell + one wall per sealed cavity), confirmed by the 0-void case giving exactly 1 and the 63-void fully-sealed case converging toward 64 (=63+1) at higher resolution; voids that breach the surface (penetration>0) merge their inner wall into the outer shell, reducing the count (74 voids, penetration=0.3 -> 27 components). This means 'connected components' means something different in carve (outer shell + hidden internal cavity walls, NOT necessarily separate printable pieces) vs fill (literally separate physical pieces) -- documented in README, left as a UI wording gap for Next. Verified end to end in isolated Chrome (port 5185, real elementFromPoint hit-tested clicks + real PointerEvent dispatch on canvas, no synthetic .click()): mode toggle button, pack button, view-mode buttons all real-coordinate-clicked; manual void add and click-select+Delete verified in both raymarch and bead views and both modes; STL watertight held across all tested configurations; history export->import byte-for-byte entries match including mode; fps via the same document.hidden-safe benchmarkRender(n) pattern skin introduced (0.101ms/frame at 1530 voids in beads, CPU-submission lower bound only, monitor-sync smoothness left for author's own visual check); all 8 existing pages (index/gravity/sag/mpm/foam/rings/skin + pack itself) console-error-free; npm run build passes with PackMode threaded through compositeSdf/raymarchComposite/buildPackMesh and the new PackRenderer/UiHandles methods.

T9 initial implementation: new Study S-pack. Host = S1 ball list + k (grow / S1 recipe import, unchanged from cloud-sculpt/field.ts). Void = a second ball list, packed greedily by rejection sampling inside the host's bounding box (field.ts's packVoidsGreedy): placeable radius at a sampled point = min(maxR, distance-to-existing-voids - gap, distance-to-host-surface - gap + penetration), rejected below minR, stopping early after a run of consecutive failures. Composite SDF = Quilez smooth subtraction opSmoothSubtraction(voidField, hostField, roundK) = smooth(max(host, -void)), one roundness knob reused for both the void-void union and the subtraction itself. New op packVoids carries its resulting void list explicitly (freeze/seedMesh precedent), so replay never re-runs the RNG walk. Manual void add (click while in add-void mode, host-only raymarch target) and click-select+Delete for removal -- no dragging at all, a deliberate scope cut to sidestep the differential-drag bug class rings/README.md documents. Gauges (estimateThinnestWall, estimateFillRatio) computed on-demand after state mutations, not per frame. Own recipe format (studyId 'pack', host+void+params) since S1's recipe cannot represent a void -- this Study is the first to extend the 正本's vocabulary. Mesh export reuses cloud-sculpt's buildMeshFromField unchanged. Bug found and fixed during verification: the surface constraint originally omitted `- gap`, so a void could become tangent to the host skin even at penetration=0, and roundK (initially 0.15) would visually round that tangent point into a pinhole despite the SDF staying closed -- fixed by subtracting gap from the surface term too, and tuned defaults to gap=0.05/roundK=0.04 (roundK <= gap) so the first-load state reads as a genuinely closed shell. Verified in isolated Chrome (port 5185): closed shell at penetration=0 (48 voids, watertight at res 64/96/128), openings emerge at penetration=0.25 (62 voids, hasOpening=true), heavy perforation at gap=0.008-0.012/attempts=6000-8000 (521-565 voids, 60-67% fill, watertight held at all tested resolutions) though a true skeleton-only state (full shell loss) was not reached in this pass -- documented honestly as open work. Added nav links to/from all 6 existing pages.
